title: This play is crazy tbh, but not in the ways I expected! #theatre #pla...
transcript: what sort of play is 3 hours long but puts the intermission 2 hours in? that's one of several things that made me wildly curious to see this audacious, divisive new play for myself and “divisive” is the right word the Show-Score ratings are all basically 5 stars or 1 star the play is called Practice by Nazareth Hassan and in a few ways it reminded me of the Tony-winning hit Stereophonic not just because it premiered at the same theatre but because they're both 3 hour plays that follow a rigorous, punishing creative process fraught with power struggles and emotional abuse but this play, about an experimental theatre troupe, has, I would say, more surprises in store and somewhat more to say. It straddles this line between drama and satire where it is genuinely disturbing but I have to admit there's also something darkly funny about the increasingly twisted and absurd ways that this imposing leader torments these poor artists and yes I went in questioning why the hell they put the intermission 2 hours in but the structure is actually very important and completely earned it throws multiple wrenches in whatever you thought you knew about the play up until that point and on a fundamental level all of the challenges that this play poses for its audience feel supported by a very high level of craft in both the writing and direction I'm saying it now: Practice is one of the best plays of the year it's gonna end up being one of the best plays of the season you have until December 7th to catch it at Playwrights Horizons although really, I think it deserves another run
